html:
Implant-Supported Bridges in Wauwatosa

Missing several teeth in a row can make everyday activities like eating, speaking, and smiling more difficult. While a traditional dental bridge can replace multiple missing teeth, it typically relies on neighboring natural teeth for support. An implant-supported bridge offers another option by using dental implants placed in the jaw to support your replacement teeth.

At MidTown Dental Care, we provide implant-supported bridges in Wauwatosa as part of our comprehensive dental implant services. Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide coordinated implant care from your initial evaluation and advanced imaging through bone grafting when necessary, implant placement, and your final restoration.

For patients missing multiple adjacent teeth, an implant-supported bridge can restore the appearance of the smile while creating a strong, stable solution for everyday function.

Schedule a Dental Implant Consultation

What Is an Implant-Supported Bridge?

An implant-supported bridge is a dental restoration used to replace multiple missing teeth. Instead of relying on neighboring natural teeth for support, the bridge is anchored by dental implants placed in the jawbone.

The implants serve as artificial tooth roots and provide a stable foundation for the restoration above the gumline.

One important advantage is that you do not necessarily need one dental implant for every missing tooth.

For example, depending on the location of the missing teeth, bone availability, bite forces, and other clinical considerations, strategically positioned implants may be able to support a bridge that replaces several teeth.

Your MidTown Dental Care dentist will determine the appropriate number and position of implants based on your individual needs.

When Is an Implant-Supported Bridge Used?

An implant-supported bridge is generally considered when two or more neighboring teeth are missing.

It may be an option if you:

  • Have several missing teeth next to one another
  • Have teeth that cannot be saved and need to be removed
  • Want a fixed alternative to a removable partial denture.
  • Prefer not to use healthy neighboring teeth to support a traditional bridge.
  • Have sufficient bone to support dental implants.
  • Are willing to complete the implant placement and healing process
  • Want a stable, long-term approach to replacing multiple teeth.

Because every patient’s smile is different, determining whether an implant-supported bridge is appropriate requires a comprehensive examination and imaging.

Benefits of Implant-Supported Bridges

Replacing multiple missing teeth can improve much more than the appearance of your smile.

Replace Several Teeth With a Fixed Restoration

An implant-supported bridge remains securely attached to dental implants rather than being removed each day, as with a conventional removable partial denture.

This can provide greater stability for everyday activities such as eating and speaking.

Preserve Healthy Neighboring Teeth

A traditional tooth-supported bridge generally requires the teeth on either side of the missing space to be prepared for crowns.

An implant-supported bridge receives its support from dental implants instead. When the neighboring teeth are healthy, they can remain intact rather than being prepared solely to support the bridge.

Restore Chewing Function

Several missing teeth can make it difficult to chew comfortably and may cause you to favor another part of your mouth.

A stable implant-supported restoration is designed to restore function in the area of the missing teeth.

Support the Jawbone

Natural tooth roots transfer biting forces into the jawbone. When teeth are lost, the bone in those areas can begin to change.

Dental implants are positioned within the jaw and transfer forces to the surrounding bone. This can help maintain bone in areas where implants are placed.

Restore Your Smile

Missing multiple teeth can have a significant effect on your appearance and confidence.

Your implant-supported bridge is designed to restore the missing portion of your smile while working with your remaining natural teeth.

Implant-Supported Bridge vs. Traditional Dental Bridge

One of the most common questions we hear is: What is the difference between an implant-supported bridge and a traditional bridge?

The primary difference is what supports the restoration.

A traditional dental bridge generally uses natural teeth on either side of the missing space as anchors. Those teeth are prepared for crowns, and the replacement tooth or teeth are connected between them.

An implant-supported bridge is anchored to dental implants positioned within the jawbone. The implants support the bridge rather than relying on adjacent natural teeth.

Neither treatment is automatically the right choice for every patient.

A traditional bridge may be a good option when the neighboring teeth already require crowns, when implant surgery is not recommended, or when other clinical circumstances make conventional bridge treatment preferable.

An implant-supported bridge may be particularly attractive when the neighboring teeth are healthy, and the patient wants an independent, implant-based restoration.

During your consultation, we can compare the two options based on your oral health, bone structure, remaining teeth, treatment goals, timeline, and budget.

Implant-Supported Bridge vs. Individual Dental Implants

If you are missing three teeth, do you need three dental implants?

Not always.

Replacing every missing tooth with an individual implant and crown may be appropriate in certain situations. In others, fewer strategically positioned implants can support a bridge that replaces several teeth.

The best solution depends on factors including:

  • Number of missing teeth
  • Location of the missing teeth
  • Available jawbone
  • Space between remaining teeth
  • Bite forces
  • Condition of surrounding teeth
  • Gum health
  • Esthetic considerations
  • Overall treatment goals

Our doctors evaluate these factors before recommending the number and position of implants.

The goal is not simply to place as many implants as possible. It is to create a well-planned restoration that provides appropriate support, function, cleansability, and appearance.

What Is the Implant-Supported Bridge Process?

Because implant-supported bridges involve both implant surgery and restorative dentistry, treatment generally occurs in stages.

At MidTown Dental Care, these stages can be coordinated within a single practice.

1. Consultation and Examination

Your treatment begins with a comprehensive evaluation.

We examine your teeth, gums, missing-tooth area, bite, and overall oral health. We will also discuss your medical history, concerns, and goals for replacing your missing teeth.

2. Advanced 3D Imaging

Detailed imaging allows our doctors to evaluate the underlying jawbone and surrounding anatomy.

This is particularly important when planning multiple-tooth replacement because the implants must be positioned to provide appropriate support for the final bridge.

3. Personalized Treatment Planning

We determine the number and intended location of the implants and plan the restoration they will eventually support.

Thinking about the final bridge from the beginning allows the surgical and restorative phases of treatment to work together.

4. Extractions or Bone Grafting When Needed

If damaged teeth are still present, extractions may be necessary.

Some patients also require bone grafting if there is insufficient healthy bone at the planned implant sites. This can be more common when teeth have been missing for an extended period.

MidTown Dental Care provides bone grafting as part of our comprehensive implant services when it is appropriate for the treatment plan.

5. Dental Implant Placement

The planned implants are surgically positioned within the jawbone.

MidTown Dental Care also offers Yomi robot-assisted dental implant technology, which provides real-time guidance based on the digital implant plan while the dentist remains in control of the procedure.

6. Healing and Integration

After placement, the implants need time to heal and integrate with the surrounding bone.

Healing time varies based on your health, bone quality, number of implants, implant location, and whether additional procedures were performed.

7. Final Implant-Supported Bridge

Once the implants have achieved adequate stability, we can proceed with your final bridge.

The restoration is designed to replace your missing teeth and restore the appearance and function of your smile.

Advanced Yomi Technology for Implant-Supported Bridges

Planning implant position is especially important when implants will work together to support a bridge.

MidTown Dental Care uses Yomi robot-assisted technology as part of our advanced approach to dental implant surgery.

Detailed digital planning allows the dentist to determine the intended implant position before surgery. During placement, Yomi provides real-time guidance and haptic feedback to help the dentist follow the planned location, angle, and depth.

The technology does not perform implant surgery independently. Your dentist performs and controls the procedure while Yomi acts as an advanced guidance system.

Patients who want to learn more about the technology can visit our Yomi Robot-Assisted Dental Implants page.

Comprehensive Implant Care With an Experienced Team

Dental implant treatment requires careful coordination between the surgical placement of the implants and the restoration they will ultimately support.

At MidTown Dental Care, our team includes Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego. Our doctors combine decades of dental experience with modern imaging and implant technology to create individualized treatment plans for patients with missing teeth.

Dr. Russell has more than 20 years of experience in dentistry and has helped incorporate advanced technologies into MidTown Dental Care. Dr. Hoyme brings more than 15 years of experience and completed a general practice residency following dental school. Dr. Schmidt is a graduate of Marquette University School of Dentistry and completed a general practice residency at Loyola University in Chicago. Dr. Crego brings more than 40 years of dental experience and has a particular interest in dental implant placement and crown-and-bridge dentistry.

Most importantly, MidTown Dental Care can coordinate your treatment from implant placement through your final restoration, including bone grafting when needed.

How Much Does an Implant-Supported Bridge Cost?

The cost of an implant-supported bridge varies because the treatment is customized to the patient.

Factors that can affect your total treatment cost include:

  • Number of missing teeth
  • Number of implants required
  • Location of the missing teeth
  • Need for tooth extractions.
  • Need for bone grafting.
  • Complexity of implant placement
  • Type of final bridge
  • Dental insurance benefits
  • Individual oral health needs

An implant-supported bridge may have a different initial cost than a traditional bridge because implant surgery is part of the treatment.

However, the initial price is only one factor to consider when comparing your options. The condition of neighboring teeth, long-term maintenance, bone support, and your overall treatment goals are also important.

After completing your evaluation, our team will provide a personalized treatment plan and explain the associated costs.

Financing Implant-Supported Bridge Treatment

MidTown Dental Care offers several options to help make dental treatment more manageable.

Financing options include CareCredit, Cherry, and Sunbit, along with in-house financing for certain procedures.

Please contact our team to discuss current dental benefits and payment options. Dental insurance coverage for implant treatment varies, so our team can help you understand applicable benefits and review available payment options.

Missing Several Teeth? Let’s Talk About Your Options.

Schedule a consultation at MidTown Dental Care to compare implant-supported bridges and other tooth-replacement solutions.

Schedule Your Dental Implant Consultation

Implant-Supported Bridge FAQs

How many implants are needed for an implant-supported bridge?

The number of implants depends on how many teeth are missing, where they are located, available bone, bite forces, and the design of the final restoration. You do not necessarily need one implant for every missing tooth. Your dentist will determine the appropriate number during treatment planning.

Can two dental implants replace three missing teeth?

In some situations, two appropriately positioned implants may support a bridge that replaces three teeth. Whether this approach is appropriate depends on the location of the teeth, bone availability, bite forces, implant position, and other clinical factors.

Is an implant-supported bridge better than a traditional bridge?

Neither option is universally better. An implant-supported bridge is supported by implants and generally does not require healthy neighboring teeth to be prepared as anchors. A traditional bridge may be preferable when neighboring teeth already need crowns, or implant treatment is not recommended.

How long does an implant-supported bridge last?

Dental implants and implant-supported restorations are designed for long-term use, but longevity varies. Oral hygiene, gum health, bite forces, smoking, general health, and regular professional care can all influence long-term success. The bridge itself may eventually require maintenance or replacement due to normal wear.

Is an implant-supported bridge removable?

Implant-supported bridges are generally designed as fixed restorations rather than something the patient removes each day. Your dentist can explain the specific restoration recommended for your situation.

Do I need bone grafting for an implant-supported bridge?

Not every patient needs bone grafting. If there is insufficient healthy bone in an area where an implant needs to be placed, grafting may be recommended to improve support. Advanced imaging helps us evaluate bone before treatment.

How do I clean under an implant-supported bridge?

Implant-supported bridges require daily cleaning around the implants and underneath the restoration. Depending on the design, floss threaders, interdental brushes, water flossers, or other cleaning aids may be recommended. Regular professional dental care is also important.

Can I get an implant-supported bridge if my teeth have been missing for years?

Possibly. Having missing teeth for a long time does not automatically prevent implant treatment. However, the bone can change after tooth loss, so additional procedures, such as bone grafting, may be necessary. A clinical examination and imaging are needed to determine candidacy.

How long does it take to get an implant-supported bridge?

Treatment length varies. The process includes implant planning and placement, a healing period, and the completion of the final restoration. Extractions, bone grafting, and individual healing can extend the timeline. We can provide a more personalized estimate after your evaluation.

Who is a good candidate for an implant-supported bridge?

Candidates generally need appropriate oral and overall health, healthy gums, sufficient bone or the ability to undergo grafting, and a commitment to maintaining good oral hygiene. Your medical history, medications, smoking status, and other factors will also be considered.

Replace Multiple Missing Teeth With a Stable Solution

You do not have to settle for gaps in your smile or assume that a removable restoration is your only option.

An implant-supported bridge can replace several missing teeth using dental implants for support, helping restore function and appearance without depending on healthy neighboring teeth as anchors.

At MidTown Dental Care, Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide comprehensive implant care in one convenient location. From advanced imaging and bone grafting when necessary to implant placement and your final restoration, our team can coordinate each stage of your care.

If you are considering an implant-supported bridge in Wauwatosa, schedule a consultation with MidTown Dental Care at 8726 W. North Ave., Wauwatosa, WI 53226. We’ll evaluate your smile, discuss your options, and create a personalized plan for replacing your missing teeth.

html:
Implant-Supported Dentures in Wauwatosa

Dentures can restore a smile after extensive tooth loss, but traditional removable dentures do not always provide the stability patients want. If your dentures move when you eat, make speaking uncomfortable, or leave you worried about smiling in social situations, dental implants may provide another option. Implant-supported dentures in Wauwatosa use dental implants to provide additional support for a denture, creating a more secure and confident way to replace multiple or all missing teeth.

At MidTown Dental Care, we provide comprehensive dental implant care in one convenient location. Our doctors At MidTown Dental Care, Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide comprehensive implant care in one convenient location. Our team can coordinate your treatment from advanced imaging and treatment planning through extractions or bone grafting when needed, implant placement, and your final restoration.

Whether you already wear dentures or are beginning to explore your options for replacing a full arch of teeth, we can help you understand whether implant-supported dentures are right for you.

Schedule a Dental Implant Consultation

What Are Implant-Supported Dentures?

Implant-supported dentures are restorations that replace multiple or all missing teeth while receiving support from dental implants placed in the jawbone.

Traditional dentures rest primarily on the gums and underlying tissues. Implant-supported dentures use strategically positioned dental implants to provide additional support and stability.

The dental implants function as artificial tooth roots. Once they have healed and integrated with the surrounding bone, they can help anchor the restoration.

The exact design of an implant-supported denture varies. Some restorations are removable by the patient for cleaning, while others may be designed to remain attached and be removed by a dental professional when necessary.

During your consultation at MidTown Dental Care, we can explain the options appropriate for your mouth, oral health, and treatment goals.

Why Do Traditional Dentures Become Loose?

A denture that once fit comfortably may become less stable over time.

One reason is that the jawbone naturally changes after teeth are lost. Tooth roots normally transfer forces into the jawbone during biting and chewing. When the teeth and roots are no longer present, the bone in those areas can gradually decrease.

As the shape of the jaw and gum tissues changes, a traditional denture may no longer fit as closely as it once did.

Patients may notice:

  • Dentures moving while eating.
  • Clicking or shifting when speaking
  • Difficulty chewing certain foods
  • Sore or irritated areas
  • Increasing reliance on denture adhesive
  • Changes in the way the denture fits
  • Feeling self-conscious when talking or smiling

A loose denture should always be evaluated. In some cases, adjustment, relining, or replacement may help. For patients seeking greater stability, dental implants may offer an alternative.

Benefits of Implant-Supported Dentures

Adding dental implant support can change the way a denture functions and feels.

Greater Stability

One of the primary reasons patients consider implant-supported dentures is stability.

Dental implants create anchor points for the restoration, which can reduce unwanted movement compared with a traditional denture that relies primarily on the gums for support.

Improved Confidence When Eating

Loose dentures can make patients cautious about what they eat or cause them to chew primarily on one side of the mouth.

A more stable restoration can improve chewing efficiency and help patients feel more confident during meals. Your individual ability to eat certain foods will still depend on the restoration, oral health, and other factors.

More Confidence When Speaking and Smiling

Concern about a denture moving can make normal conversations stressful.

Improved stability can reduce some of the movement associated with conventional dentures, allowing patients to speak and smile with greater confidence.

Less Dependence on Denture Adhesive

Some traditional denture wearers use adhesive to improve retention.

An implant-supported restoration receives additional support from implants, potentially reducing reliance on adhesives. The amount of support depends on the specific restoration and implant configuration.

Jawbone Support

Dental implants are positioned within the jawbone and transfer forces to the surrounding bone during function.

While dental implants do not prevent all age-related or anatomical changes in the jaw, they can help maintain bone in the areas where implants are placed.

Implant-Supported Dentures vs. Traditional Dentures

Patients frequently ask whether implant-supported dentures are better than traditional dentures.

The biggest difference is how the denture is supported.

Traditional dentures generally rest on the gums and underlying tissues. Upper dentures may also use suction across the palate for retention.

Implant-supported dentures receive additional support from dental implants anchored within the jaw.

This can provide improved stability, particularly during chewing and speaking.

However, traditional dentures remain an appropriate treatment for many patients. They do not require implant surgery, generally involve a lower initial investment, and can restore an entire arch of missing teeth.

Implant-supported dentures require sufficient bone or the ability to prepare the jaw for implants, surgical treatment, a healing period, and a larger initial investment.

The right option depends on your health, anatomy, expectations, budget, and priorities.

How Many Dental Implants Are Needed to Support a Denture?

There is no single number that applies to every patient.

The number of implants needed depends on factors including:

  • Upper or lower jaw
  • Available jawbone
  • Bone quality
  • Shape and size of the jaw
  • Type of denture or restoration
  • Bite forces
  • Location of available bone
  • Overall oral health
  • Whether the restoration will be removable or fixed
  • Treatment goals

Some implant-supported dentures can be stabilized with fewer implants, while other full-arch restorations require additional implants to provide the planned support.

Rather than starting with a predetermined number, our doctors evaluate your anatomy and determine the implant configuration that is appropriate for your restoration.

Can I Get Dental Implants If I Already Wear Dentures?

Potentially, yes.

Many patients explore implant-supported dentures after wearing traditional dentures for years.

However, patients who have been missing teeth for a long time may have experienced changes in the jawbone. That does not automatically mean dental implants are no longer possible.

Advanced imaging allows us to evaluate the amount and location of available bone. If additional support is necessary, bone grafting may be incorporated into the treatment plan when appropriate.

Your existing denture, oral health, bone, medical history, and treatment goals all need to be evaluated before determining the best approach.

What Is the Implant-Supported Denture Process?

Implant-supported denture treatment involves several stages. Because MidTown Dental Care provides comprehensive implant care, these stages can be coordinated within one practice.

1. Comprehensive Consultation

We begin by discussing what you want to improve.

If you already wear dentures, tell us what is working and what is not. Difficulty chewing, looseness, sore areas, concerns about appearance, and reliance on adhesive are all important considerations.

If you still have teeth remaining, we evaluate their condition and determine whether they can be maintained or extraction should be considered.

2. Advanced 3D Imaging

Detailed imaging helps our doctors evaluate your jawbone and surrounding anatomy.

We assess the available bone and begin planning potential implant locations based on the restoration the implants will ultimately support.

3. Personalized Treatment Planning

Implant-supported denture treatment should be planned with the final restoration in mind.

Our doctors determine the appropriate implant configuration and explain any preparatory treatment that may be needed.

You will also have an opportunity to discuss the expected treatment sequence, healing process, restoration, and financial considerations before moving forward.

4. Extractions and Bone Grafting When Needed

Some patients need remaining damaged or failing teeth removed before implant treatment.

Bone grafting may also be recommended if additional bone support is needed in planned implant areas.

MidTown Dental Care can provide extractions, bone grafting, implant placement, and restorative treatment as part of your coordinated plan.

5. Dental Implant Placement

The dental implants are surgically placed at the planned locations in your jaw.

Our team also offers Yomi robot-assisted dental implant technology to provide real-time guidance during implant surgery based on the digital treatment plan.

6. Healing

The implants need time to integrate with the surrounding bone.

Healing time varies from patient to patient and depends on the number and location of implants, bone quality, overall health, and whether additional procedures were performed.

Our team will explain what you can expect at this stage and, when applicable, what type of restoration may be used during treatment.

7. Your Implant-Supported Denture

After the implants have achieved adequate stability, treatment can proceed with the planned restoration.

Your final denture is designed around your mouth, smile, bite, and implant positions to restore missing teeth and provide the planned level of support.

Yomi Robot-Assisted Technology for Denture Implant Treatment

When multiple implants will work together to support a restoration, careful implant planning is especially important.

MidTown Dental Care uses Yomi robot-assisted dental implant technology to support implant placement.

Detailed imaging and digital treatment planning allow the intended implant positions to be established before surgery. During the procedure, Yomi provides the dentist with real-time guidance and haptic feedback based on that plan.

The robot does not perform the surgery independently. Your MidTown Dental Care dentist remains in control of the procedure while using Yomi as an advanced guidance tool.

This technology can be particularly valuable when planning several implants that must work together to support a larger restoration.

How Much Do Implant-Supported Dentures Cost?

The cost of implant-supported dentures varies because several components of treatment must be considered.

  • Number of implants required

Implant-Supported Denture FAQs

Are implant-supported dentures removable?

Some implant-supported dentures are designed so the patient can remove them for cleaning, while others are designed to remain attached and are removed by a dental professional when necessary. We can explain which options are appropriate for your needs.

How many implants do I need for implant-supported dentures?

There is no universal number. The appropriate number depends on your jaw, available bone, restoration type, bite forces, and treatment goals. Advanced imaging and treatment planning allow your dentist to determine an appropriate implant configuration.

Are implant-supported dentures better than regular dentures?

Implant-supported dentures generally provide greater stability because dental implants help anchor the restoration. Traditional dentures do not require implant surgery and may be appropriate for patients who prefer or require a nonsurgical option. The better choice depends on your individual circumstances.

Can I convert my existing dentures to implant-supported dentures?

Sometimes an existing denture can potentially be incorporated into implant treatment, but many patients require a new restoration designed specifically for their implants. Your dentist needs to evaluate the fit, condition, design, and strength of your current denture before determining whether it can be used.

Can I get implant-supported dentures if I have bone loss?

Bone loss does not automatically prevent implant treatment. The amount and location of remaining bone must be evaluated with appropriate imaging. Bone grafting or other modifications to the treatment plan may be recommended depending on your anatomy.

Do implant-supported dentures feel more like natural teeth?

Implant support can provide greater stability than conventional dentures, particularly during chewing and speaking. However, an implant-supported denture is still a dental prosthesis and will not feel exactly like natural teeth.

Do implant-supported dentures need adhesive?

Many implant-supported restorations receive their retention and stability from the dental implants rather than relying primarily on denture adhesive. Whether any additional products are needed depends on the specific restoration.

How long do implant-supported dentures last?

Dental implants are designed for long-term use, but both the implants and restoration require ongoing care. The denture itself can experience wear and may eventually require adjustment, maintenance, repair, or replacement. Oral hygiene, smoking, health, bite forces, and professional dental care can affect longevity.

How do you clean implant-supported dentures?

Cleaning requirements depend on whether your restoration is removable or fixed. Daily cleaning around the implants and restoration is essential. Your dental team may recommend specialized brushes, flossing aids, a water flosser, or other tools based on your restoration.

Am I too old for implant-supported dentures?

Age alone does not determine whether someone can receive dental implants. Overall health, healing ability, medications, jawbone, gum health, and other factors are more important. Healthy older adults may still be candidates for implant treatment after an appropriate evaluation.

Tired of Restless Sleep? Obstructive Sleep Apnea Treatment Can Help

Do you feel chronically tired due to restless sleep? Or do you grind your teeth and snore at night? If so, it can be difficult to pin down what is causing these occurrences as well as frustrating since the negative effects of a lack of sleep build up over time. In many cases, we at MidTown Dental Care in Wauwatosa have found these unpleasant experiences can be addressed through Obstructive Sleep Apnea treatment.

Do you feel chronically tired due to restless sleep? Or do you grind your teeth and snore at night? If so, it can be difficult to pin down what is causing these occurrences as well as frustrating since the negative effects of a lack of sleep build up over time. In many cases, we at MidTown Dental Care in Wauwatosa have found these unpleasant experiences can be addressed through Obstructive Sleep Apnea treatment.

Obstructive Sleep Apnea is a sleep disorder that involves breathing disruptions. This disorder is caused by intermittent relaxation of the throat muscles, which can lead to blockage of the upper airways. This intermittent blockage causes a person’s breathing to repeatedly stop and start again during sleep. Due to the dangers of breath cessation, this disorder can be quite serious. 

You may not know if you are suffering from Obstructive Sleep Apnea unless you know what signs to look out for. There are many Obstructive Sleep apnea symptoms, including excessive snoring, headaches, frequent daytime fatigue, increased anxiety or depression, irritability, memory loss, high blood pressure, and even gastric reflux. Additionally, as a result of fatigue and sleep loss, people suffering from sleep apnea often develop a reliance on sleep aids. 

Diagnosis & Treatment 

At MidTown Dental Care, we will conduct your initial consultation and provide you with a Home Sleep Test (HST). The HST is sent to a sleep physician, who reads and interprets the data that was taken during your night’s sleep. Our team will then review the results of the test to determine if you would benefit from an oral sleep appliance.

Generally, the treatment options will be between a CPAP machine and an Oral Sleep Appliance, with the latter option being the most common. An Oral Sleep Appliance is a device you wear in your mouth while sleeping to bring your jaw forward and open up your airway. The opening of the airway leads to better, less obstructed sleep and can alleviate many symptoms described above.

Once we have determined that you will likely benefit from this device, we will construct one specially to fit your mouth comfortably. Usually, it takes about a month from review of your initial Home Sleep Test to provide you with your Oral Sleep Appliance.    

Book An Appointment For Obstructive Sleep Apnea Treatment

If you are tired, frequently feel foggy headed in the morning, are noticing wear on your teeth, or have been told that you snore loudly, it’s time to check if you are suffering from Obstructive Sleep Apnea. Book an appointment at MidTown Dental Care today to start getting relief through Obstructive Sleep Apnea treatment!

How Teeth Whitening Works at MidTown Dental Care

We offer two reliable whitening methods, and both deliver noticeable results. Depending on your schedule and preferences, we’ll help you choose the option that fits best:

In-Office Whitening

Take-Home Whitening

Common Questions About Whitening

Is professional whitening safe?

Absolutely. When supervised by a dentist, whitening is both gentle and effective. We monitor the process closely to protect your teeth and gums.

How long will my results last?

Most patients enjoy a brighter smile for six to twelve months with proper care and regular cleanings. Touch-ups can extend your results even further.

Will I experience sensitivity?

Some people notice mild, temporary sensitivity. If that happens, we’ll suggest products and techniques to help you stay comfortable.

Can whitening damage my teeth?

Not when done professionally. Our dental technology and techniques are designed to protect your enamel while delivering the results you want.

MidTown Dental Membership Guidelines

The MidTown Dental Membership is not insurance. The program is offered to individuals and families who do not have insurance, or who choose not to utilize their insurance. This dental membership cannot be used along with an insurance plan or CareCredit. Benefits are not transferable to another dental practice or dental specialty practice.

Contact our office to discuss current membership fees, enrollment and which option fits your needs.

How membership works

  • Membership is for one year, beginning on the enrollment date.
  • New patients meet the team and have a dental assessment.
  • Payment options include paying for the year or a one-time activation fee followed by monthly payments.
  • Membership dues are non-refundable.
  • Cash, check or credit card payments are accepted.
  • Membership automatically renews on the anniversary date unless a written cancellation request is received 30 days before renewal.
  • Membership must be current to receive discounts.
  • Additional services are the member’s responsibility and are due on the date of service to qualify for discounts.
  • Fees for dental services may change.
  • Members are responsible for scheduling and keeping appointments included in the program.

Benefits and exclusions

The membership has no deductibles, pre-authorizations, yearly maximums or waiting period.

Exclusions include implants, Invisalign, SureSmile, clear aligner therapy and sleep appliances. Please review the current program details with our team before enrolling.

Accessibility Statement for midtowndentalcare.org

MidTown Dental Care is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We are continually improving the user experience for everyone and applying the relevant accessibility standards.

Conformance status

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) defines requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA.

MidTown Dental Care is making constant efforts to improve the accessibility of its site and services in the belief that it is our collective moral obligation to allow seamless, accessible, and unhindered use for those of us with disabilities.

We aim to make all pages and content on midtowndentalcare.org accessible, but some content may not yet fully meet the highest accessibility standards. This could be due to challenges in identifying the most suitable technological solution.

We may revise this Statement periodically to reflect improvements or changes to our accessibility practices.

Feedback

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of MidTown Dental Care website. Please let us know if you encounter accessibility barriers on our website:

E-mail: frontdesk@midtowndentalcare.net

We try to respond to feedback within 3–5 business days.
